name: Aghu Tharnggalu
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Paman; only Alpher 2016 subclassification notes and AIATSIS wordlist-level materials surfaced; no grammar/phonology found.

sources.citation: Sutton, Peter & Ken Hale. 2021. Linguistic Organisation and Native Title: The Wik Case, Australia. Canberra: ANU Press, ch. 7, pp. 205-213
sources.note: Discusses Aghu Tharrnggala atonic pronouns (from Jolly 1989) that 'differ from full pronouns in accent only', examples marked with a grave accent (e.g. 'yàw', 'nành'); no rule for where word stress falls.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Aghu Tharrnggala language' (accessed 2026-09-17); PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory ER 2880 (Round, source 'Jolly nd'); Grambank aghu1254 (source Jolly 1989); Glottolog reference 73578
sources.note: Wikipedia gives consonant and vowel tables (7 vowels incl. ɨ, ə) but no statement on stress; PHOIBLE lists 27 segments, no suprasegmentals; Grambank codes no stress feature; Glottolog record confirms Jolly 1989 = BA Hons thesis, iii+186 pp., listed by Glottolog as a grammar sketch.

sources.citation: Verstraete, Jean-Christophe. 2018. 'Perhaps' in Cape York Peninsula. In Daniel Van Olmen, Tanja Mortelmans & Frank Brisard (eds), Aspects of Linguistic Variation, 247-268. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton (open access, OAPEN 20.500.12657/59553)
sources.note: Uses Aghu Tharrnggala data from Jolly 1989 (pp. 54, 104: apprehensive 'me', 'ta-ng' 'see!/perhaps') for epistemic marking; nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Sommer, Bruce A. 1969. Kunjen phonology: synchronic and diachronic. Pacific Linguistics B-11
sources.note: Names 'Koko-Mini and Aghu Tharnggalai' only in Hale's classification list; nothing on Aghu Tharrnggala stress.

sources.citation: Hale, Kenneth. 1966. The Paman group of the Pama-Nyungan phylic family (Appendix to XXIX). In G.N. O'Grady, C.F. Voegelin & F.M. Voegelin, Languages of the World: Indo-Pacific fascicle six, Anthropological Linguistics 8(2), p. 54
sources.note: 'Aghu Tharnggala' appears only in the Southern Pama subgroup listing; no phonology.

sources.citation: Jolly, Lesley. 1989. Aghu Tharrnggala: a language of the Princess Charlotte Bay region of Cape York Peninsula. BA (Hons) thesis, University of Queensland, iii+186 pp. (phonology chapter; 'acoustic analysis')
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
